comments.note: project-detail-dialogues.js line 274: tab click guard uses `btn.className.indexOf('dialogue-tab') === -1`. If a child element is ever added inside a tab button, e.target would not be the button and the guard would falsely reject valid tab clicks. This is safe for the current markup (text-only buttons) but would silently break if child elements are added. Consider using e.target.closest('.dialogue-tab') for future-proofing — consistent with the existing .closest('.dialogue-tool-toggle') pattern two lines below.

API.getChunkText() has no dedicated unit test in api-client.test.ts. The method is exercised indirectly via the api-chunk-text server-side tests, but a frontend unit test asserting the URL pattern and data.content extraction would match the pattern for getChunkRendered and getChunkStructured which do have dedicated tests (verified at api-client.test.ts lines for getChunkRendered/getChunkStructured). Recommend adding 2-3 tests: URL construction, URI encoding of all three params, and data.content extraction.

The tab bar interaction (two-tab switch, lazy-load on first Text Only click, cache reuse on second click) has no automated unit test in project-detail-dialogues.test.ts. The existing test suite covers _openDialogueModal legacy path (AC-8) and chunk-priority rendering but not the useChunks=true tab UI. Recommend adding tests for: tab bar presence, active class toggling, first-click fetch call, second-click cache hit (getChunkText not called twice), and error state rendering in textOnlyPanel.

When API.getChunkText() is called and fails, the catch sets textOnlyPanel.innerHTML to an error message (line 307). However, cachedTextHtml remains null, meaning a second click on Text Only would re-attempt the fetch (not reuse the error message). This is arguably correct behavior (retry on error) but worth documenting — it differs from the success path where cache is permanent.

Fix-Forward applied: tab-click guard on line 274 changed from btn.className.indexOf('dialogue-tab') === -1 to e.target.closest('.dialogue-tab') — consistent with the .closest('.dialogue-tool-toggle') pattern already used on line 329. Non-behavioral: the tab buttons contain only text so no functional difference, but the approach is now resilient to future button child elements and idiomatic with the rest of the file.

comments.note: project-detail-dialogues.js line 274: tab-click guard changed from `btn.className.indexOf('dialogue-tab') === -1` to `e.target.closest('.dialogue-tab')`. The old guard treats e.target directly as the button — if a child element is ever added inside a tab button (e.g., an icon span), e.target would be the child and className.indexOf would falsely reject the click. The `.closest()` API traverses up to the nearest matching ancestor, making it resilient to child elements. Non-behavioral for the current markup (text-only buttons). This also makes the tab-bar handler idiomatic with the tool-toggle handler at line 329, which already uses `.closest('.dialogue-tool-toggle')`.

project-detail-dialogues.js line 265: `textOnlyPanel.style.cssText = detailedPanel.style.cssText` copies inline styles that are empty at construction time (both panels share the .dialogue-modal-body class; no inline styles are set). This is a no-op — harmless, but unnecessary. Could be simplified to omit the cssText copy entirely. Not applied as Fix-Forward since it is a very minor cleanup with zero risk benefit at this scale.
